related_questions.question: What are the CDC recommendations for HIV prevention?
related_questions.title: Key points
list: Many tools are available to help prevent HIV.
You can choose not having sex, activities with lower chances of HIV transmission, never sharing needles, and using condoms.
You can also use HIV prevention medicines such as PrEP or PEP.
If you have HIV, you can prevent transmitting HIV to others.

related_questions.question: Which age group has the highest rate of HIV transmission?

text_blocks.snippet: In the United States, the age group with the highest rate of HIV diagnoses is 25-34 years old. This group accounted for 37% of all new HIV diagnoses in 2022, according to KFF. While younger individuals (13-24) also experience high rates of new infections, the 25-34 age group has the largest number of diagnoses.

list.title: 25-34 year olds:
list.snippet: This age group consistently shows the highest number and rate of HIV diagnoses in the US.

list.title: 13-24 year olds:
list.snippet: While not the highest, this age group remains at high risk and accounts for a significant portion of new infections, with 19% of diagnoses in 2022 according to KFF.

list.title: Other age groups:
list.snippet: HIV infections also occur in older adults, but the rate is generally lower compared to the younger age groups.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that the specific patterns and rates of transmission can vary based on factors like geographic location, race/ethnicity, and sexual orientation. For example, in some regions, young gay and bisexual men are disproportionately affected.
